findings.summary: The export expands lots into a projected 1,807,231 worksheet rows, exceeding Excel's 1,048,576-row limit. Although EXCEL_MAX_ROWS is declared, it is never enforced, so the required ordinary single-sheet workbook cannot remain within worksheet capacity and may fail, truncate data, or produce an unusable export.

Nested flatMap/map calls materialize the entire expanded export as a browser-side array before writing it. At the evidenced scale of roughly 1.8 million objects, this is unbounded relative to browser memory and can prevent the default export from remaining downloadable.

unverified: Whether writeSingleBrowserWorksheet independently rejects, truncates, streams, or otherwise handles oversized input cannot be verified from the supplied diff.
Reconciliation behavior and tests proving row completeness, worksheet capacity enforcement, and successful browser download at default annual-report scale are not shown.
Definitions and runtime availability of Lot and writeSingleBrowserWorksheet are not shown, so compilation and error handling cannot be verified.

findings.summary: displayedClosing subtracts only expense and fx_eur consumption, omitting the supported fx_other category. The observed 1,494,440 TRY of fx_other consumption therefore overstates the displayed closing balance by exactly 1,494,440 TRY and violates reconciliation.

unverified: Opening, inflow, outflow, conversion, and closing display behavior for every pool consumer category cannot be verified because the supplied diff only implements a closing-balance calculation.
Test coverage, numeric representation/rounding behavior, and the definitions of Pool and sum cannot be verified from the supplied text.

findings.summary: Each detail amount is rounded independently, so rounding residuals accumulate and the returned amounts are not guaranteed to sum to the source amount; this directly violates exact cent-level reconciliation and is consistent with the reported 1578 TRY aggregate drift.
The function does not validate that shares are finite, nonnegative, or sum to 1, allowing malformed inputs to produce NaN, Infinity, negative allocations, or totals unrelated to the source.

unverified: No tests are shown for cent-level reconciliation, fractional-cent residual distribution, zero or negative sources, malformed shares, or floating-point boundary cases.

findings.summary: The verify script no longer runs `prisma generate`, so generated clients are not refreshed before typecheck after schema changes, directly violating the release-gate requirement.

The `|| echo existing Prisma mismatch` fallback converts every non-zero TypeScript result into a successful script exit, masking both Prisma-related and unrelated typecheck failures and making the release gate non-truthful.
A temporary local reviewer probe is added to the release tree despite the frozen acceptance requirement excluding reviewer probes.
Private root-cause scratch notes are added to the release tree despite the frozen acceptance requirement limiting shipment to product and durable public methodology artifacts.

unverified: Operational feasibility, correctness, scale and bounded output, reconciliation, numerical stability, generated-artifact freshness, broader error handling, security, and tests cannot be verified from the supplied two-file diff.
